summary: W4A16 MoE decode on NVFP4-CSF checkpoints now runs as fast as plain NVFP4, and GLM-5.3 runs W4A16 at TP6 (352 expert channels per rank)
details: Stage-readable NVFP4-CSF scale storage carries each atom's replacement scale words inline, so every pipeline stage copies its compressed scales without dependent reads or a per-tile prologue wait, and the scale-word rebuild overlaps the stage's MMAs; outputs stay bit-identical to native NVFP4 scales.

GLM-5.3 TP8 (256 channels per rank) fused MoE with B12X_W4A16_SMALL_M_OCCUPANCY=2, CSF vs native at 4/8/16/32/64 tokens: +12.4/+3.1/+2.7/+1.7/+1.3% before, 0.0/-0.7/-0.6/-1.4/-1.3% now. Served GLM-5.3 TP8 MTP3: the FP4-CSF checkpoint decodes within 1.5% of the original (C1 83.9 vs 85.0, C2 137.3 vs 138.7, C4 194.9 vs 196.8 steps/s).

Packed NVFP4 W4A16 (native and CSF scales) supports expert shards whose channel count is 32 mod 64, such as GLM-5.3 TP6 (2048 padded to 2112, 352 channels per rank): N64 gate/up tiles and K32 down tiles, for decode and prefill. At TP6 CSF is within +0.1% of native at 4 tokens and 0.4-0.5% faster at 8-64.
Fixes a K32 activation-tile swizzle that left its 64-byte rows and corrupted large-batch outputs of K32 W4A16 tiles.
